newsitem.title: USA: US cash prods edge up on API, East RFG stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: US cash prods edge up on API, East RFG stocks rise.

text.p: U.S. spot products prices rose narrowly in late trade on Tuesday, after the API release data reflecting normal seasonal inventory changes last week.
Heating oil prices edged up by about 0.20 cent a gallon from late afternoon assessments, while gasolines tacked on 0.25 cent from earlier, they said.

API said distillate stocks rose by 2.9 million barrels, fairly split by heating oil and diesel supplies. Heating oil stocks on the east coast, at 21.5 million barrels, were still 18.7 million barrels behind a year ago.
Total gasoline stocks fell by about 1.4 million barrels, but reformulated gasoline stocks actually rose by 1.1 million barrels in the fuel-thirsty East Coast region.
Earlier on Tuesday, U.S. spot products prices followed NYMEX to gains of about 0.75 cent a gallon at both centers, amid hightened concern over developments in Iraq.
Buyers on the futures market were sparked by report of troop movements in the nation, sending the October crude oil contract to levels just below its lifetime highs.
But cash market dealings were less than enthusiastic at both centers, with differntials slightly weaker than in previous sessions.
